title: GCG Attack Position Sensitivity: Prefix vs. Suffix vs. Interleaved Token Placement

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: if prefix attacks are more effective, current suffix-focused defenses have a gap. However, the link from position sensitivity to actionable defense improvement has a gap since it describes the problem more than a solution.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running GCG optimization (even with nanogcg) requires understanding gradient-based adversarial optimization and white-box model access with GPU-intensive computation. Advanced ML background needed.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three position variants across 3 models and multiple prompts is manageable in scope, but GCG optimization is slow and compute-intensive. 30 hours may be tight for convergence across all conditions.

novelty.reasoning: This idea is directly addressed by 'Beyond Suffixes: Token Position in GCG Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models' (arXiv:2602.03265, February 2026). That paper identifies token position as a critical blind spot, tests prefix vs. suffix placement, and shows position substantially influences attack success rates. Mask-GCG (arXiv:2509.06350, 2025) further studies which tokens in adversarial suffixes are necessary. The proposed research question — comparing prefix, suffix, and interleaved GCG token placement — is the exact topic of the 'Beyond Suffixes' paper.
